business_problem: Walmart and Unilever wanted a practical way to prepare workers for roles displaced by automation and changing business needs, but traditional role-based career planning hid transferable skills and made it difficult to identify viable pathways within or across organizations.
solution_summary: As part of a World Economic Forum future-of-work pilot, Accenture helped Walmart and Unilever build an AI-assisted talent-mobility model around skills rather than job titles. The core technology came from SkyHive, whose quantum labor analysis breaks roles into underlying skills, measures overlap between declining and emerging jobs and identifies the specific skills a worker would need to learn for a successful transition. Accenture used those outputs to build upskilling pathways and test whether people could move across functions and even between organizations in realistic time frames. The pilot ran from December 2020 to February 2021 and linked skill inference, role matching and pathway design so the companies could expose hidden capabilities, reduce bias in career planning and show managers that talent mobility can be treated as an operational business capability rather than an ad hoc HR exercise.

solution_components.name: SkyHive
solution_components.role: Analyzes labor-market supply and demand and decomposes jobs into transferable skill profiles.

solution_components.name: quantum labor analysis
solution_components.role: Measures skill overlap between declining and emerging roles to reveal realistic transition options.

solution_components.name: skill matching
solution_components.role: Maps workers to adjacent roles within and across organizations based on demonstrated capabilities.

solution_components.name: upskilling pathways
solution_components.role: Translate identified skill gaps into practical learning plans for role transitions.

data_flow: Role and labor-market data are broken into granular skill profiles by SkyHive and its quantum labor analysis engine, then compared through skill matching to identify adjacent jobs. Accenture uses those matches to build upskilling pathways that show workers and employers what training is needed for internal or cross-company moves.
integration_points: World Economic Forum Consumer Industries Task Force on the Future of Work
business_outcome: The pilot showed that AI-based skill inference can surface hidden worker capabilities, create credible transition paths and help large employers treat upskilling and cross-company mobility as a faster, more equitable response to workforce disruption.
architecture_clues: The pilot ran from December 2020 to February 2021 and centered on three explicit hypotheses about mobility and skills.
SkyHive models roles as collections of skills rather than fixed job descriptions.
Accenture turned skill matches into formal upskilling pathways instead of leaving them as analytics outputs.
The program tested both intra-company and cross-company transitions.
